title: UX Design Principles for Semi Autonomous Multi Agent Systems — Victor Dibia, Microsoft
talk_summary: Victor Dibia demos BlenderLM, a from-scratch multi-agent system that turns natural language into Blender scenes, and derives four UX/design principles for semi-autonomous agents: capability discovery, observability/provenance, interruptibility, and cost-aware delegation. He also argues for eval-driven design (goal, baseline, tools, test bed, then agent) and warns that multi-agent is only worth it for a small class of tasks.

takeaways.technique: Eval-driven build order: goal → non-agent baseline → tools → test bed → agent
takeaways.what_they_do: Before writing any agent, they define the goal, build a scripted baseline with no AI, define the tools a human would need, and build an eval harness (notebook, then interactive UI, then automated metrics) before adding the agent loop.
takeaways.evidence_quote: First, let's define the goal... come up with a baseline... we build out our tools... we define a test bed... that's when you then go ahead and build the agent.

takeaways.what_they_do: After each action, a separate verifier agent snapshots state (object list + visual) and asks an LLM whether progress is being made or the task is stalled, then decides next step.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every time this agent takes a step we just take... the content of the scene... use an LM to predict are we making progress is use a task completed

takeaways.technique: Planner agent decomposes task into atomic steps up front
takeaways.what_they_do: An incoming task is first broken by a planner agent into atomic steps, each then executed in the agent loop rather than letting the executor improvise the whole plan.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when the task came in the planner sort of broke it down into atomic steps and then each of the steps sort of addressed in this sort of type loop

takeaways.what_they_do: A module inspects each proposed action, estimates its cost/risk, and escalates to a human when the action is expensive or dangerous rather than treating all tool calls as equal.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want a module that actively inspects... and tries to estimate the cost of the action and then knows when to delegate to the user

takeaways.technique: Interruptibility: checkpoint, pause, resume, roll back
takeaways.what_they_do: Design the system so any run can be paused, checkpointed, rolled back, and resumed, because agents may go down wrong routes or consume unentitled resources.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want a system that enables things like checkpointing, roll back, pauses and resumes

takeaways.technique: Multi-agent only for a narrow task class; 5-step fit test
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues multi-agent only pays off when the task needs planning, multiple personas, large context partitioning, or adaptive reaction; otherwise use deterministic workflows.
